decisions.reason: The reference class electrometer is a home-page flagship at the core of the firm's dosimetry heritage, so its heavy visible commitment and fit with the announced direction make withdrawal very unlikely.

The oncology risk management software supports the announced shift toward integration and patient-safety prediction, so management would read slow uptake as a temporary adoption lag that does not justify reversing the earlier decision.
The CT image quality phantom builds on the established offer and fits the imaging QA line the firm promotes as a focus, so there is little reason to abandon it after one year.

Although the mammography phantom is distant from the core offer, it has its own page and belongs to the imaging QA push the firm has publicly announced, so weak early results would be attributed to market entry effort rather than failure.

The full field mammography phantom overlaps with Product D and is far from the firm's established business, which makes it the most likely candidate for consolidation, but the firm's recent public commitment to imaging QA argues for keeping it for now.
The imaging QA instrument line is a multi-model flagship that carries the firm's announced expansion, so the investment and public commitment behind it make dropping it very unlikely.
